questions: What happens if there are no pieces initially (all A_i = 0)?
Can we choose i = 1 or i = N when moving pieces, and what does "closer" mean in those edge cases?
If multiple pieces start on the same square, do they all move together as a group during an operation?
Is it allowed to have more than one piece in a square at any time during the process?
Does the final configuration require exactly one piece per target square (B_i = 1), or just at least one?
Are operations applied sequentially or can their effects overlap in a single step?
How should ties be broken when determining the minimum number of operations if multiple sequences yield the same result?
What constitutes a valid move—can we select any index i regardless of whether there's already a piece at that position?
answers: This question addresses a different ambiguity not covered in the reference.
It refers to the minimum number of operations required
inline_prompts:
You are given two length-N strings A = A_1A_2 \ldots A_N and B = B_1B_2 \ldots B_N.
There are N squares aligned in a row from left to right. For i = 1, 2, \ldots, N, the i-th square from the left is called square i. Initially, square i contains a piece if A_i = 1, and no piece if A_i = 0.
You may repeat the following operation any number of times (possibly zero):
- Choose an integer i between 1 and N, inclusive.
- Move all pieces simultaneously one square closer to square i: if i < j, then the piece moves left to square j-1; if i > j, it moves right to square j+1; if i = j, it stays in place. 
Determine whether it is possible to reach a configuration satisfying the following condition, and if it is possible, find the number of operations needed to do so:
For every i = 1, 2, \ldots, N, there is at least one piece in square i if and only if B_i = 1.
You are given T independent test cases. Print the answer for each of them.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
T
\mathrm{case}_1
\mathrm{case}_2
\vdots
\mathrm{case}_T
Here, \mathrm{case}_i (i=1,2,\ldots,T) denotes the i-th test case.
Each test case is given in the following format:
N
A
B
Output
Print T lines.
For each i = 1, 2, \ldots, T, on the i-th line, print -1 if it is impossible to reach a configuration satisfying the condition for the i-th test case. Otherwise, print the number of operations needed.
Constraints
- 1 \leq T \leq 2 \times 10^5
- 1 \leq N \leq 10^6
- T and N are integers.
- A and B are strings of length N, each consisting of 0 and 1.
- There exists i such that A_i = 1.
- There exists i such that B_i = 1.
- The sum of N over all test cases is at most 10^6.
